name: lsp
description: Installs and launches language servers on demand, answers agent LSP queries — diagnostics, completion, hover, definition, references, symbols — for whatever file is touched, and contributes symbols, references and calls to ASP.

asp.lsp.description: The ASP provider door: {op: expand, entity} for a `file:` (its `symbol:` outline) or a `symbol:` (what references it, what it calls and what calls it), and {op: search, query, limit} for a bare name through the running servers. Answers {nodes, edges} or nil.

context.lsp.description: The catalog as evidence for the record's context collector: {op: contribute | read, query/reference}; each row is one language server with its installed state.

tool.lsp.description: The LSP tool envelope: {op: describe | call | cancel, input, context}. Input ops: status, install, diagnostics, completion, hover, definition, references, symbols. A language server missing for a touched language is installed on demand.

file.description: a workspace file, keyed as fs keys it; lsp expands it to the symbols it declares

symbol.description: a symbol a language server names: `<file key>#<container>::<name>`, with `@<line>` on a repeated name

references.description: the symbol, or the file outside any symbol, uses the target symbol

calls.description: the symbol calls the target symbol

lsp.kind.description: the symbol kind as a word: function, struct, method, …

auto_install.doc: Install a missing language server on first query, instead of reporting it missing.

cache_dir.doc: Directory holding installed language servers. Absent uses $XDG_CACHE_HOME/cartridge/lsp, then $HOME/.cache/cartridge/lsp, then $TMPDIR/cartridge-lsp.

install_timeout_ms.doc: How long one install may run before it is abandoned.

query_timeout_ms.doc: How long one LSP query (completion, hover, definition, references, symbols, diagnostics refresh) may take before it is abandoned.

max_result_bytes.doc: Bytes of one query result returned before it is truncated.

max_servers.doc: Running language-server processes kept at once; least-recently-used servers are stopped past this.
